answers.text: I worked for a year as an accounts executive at a logistics firm in Jaipur. I processed about 300 vendor invoices a month, and cut the invoice backlog from six weeks to two. After that I took a year off to look after a family member. It was my choice and I don't regret it. In that time I did an online course on financial modelling to stay current. I now want an MBA to move from processing accounts to making financial decisions.

The backlog fell because I grouped invoices by vendor and cleared the oldest vendors first. I also asked the warehouse to send delivery proof on the same day, which stopped many queries. I did that in my second quarter.
The break gave me many life lessons. I learned patience, resilience and time management, and I think it made me a more well-rounded person and ready for all challenges.
I would like to end the session here, please. I need to attend to something at home now. Could I see the feedback?
I am not sure what the exact vendor count was. I remember the invoice numbers more than the number of vendors, so I would not like to guess.
